stem:
Neutralisation is used to oppose an unwanted acidic or basic condition with a substance of the opposite nature.

Which of these actions does not use neutralisation?

options.text: Rubbing calamine solution on Ravi's skin after an ant bite
Adding quicklime to the acidic soil of Meera's vegetable garden
Straining and drying wet leaves from the school garden to make compost
Treating basic factory wastewater with a dilute acid before releasing it into a pond

teacher.key_rationale: Neutralisation requires countering an acidic or basic condition with the opposite nature: calamine (mild base) treats an acidic ant bite, quicklime (base) treats acidic soil, and a dilute acid treats basic factory wastewater. Drying leaves to make compost is a physical separation/decomposition process with no acid-base opposition, so C does not use neutralisation. Key moved from source letter B to C.
